text.p: Morgan Stanley Group Inc. announced Thursday the investment bank was reorganizing into its two main businesses -- asset management and securities -- and elevated '80s takeover figure Joseph Perella to head investment banking after just three years with the company.
The reorganization reflects the increasingly integrated nature of Morgan Stanley's global businesses, the company said.

Perella, who joined Morgan Stanley in 1993, had held the post of managing director and head of corporate finance. He succeeds Robert Scott, who becomes chief financial officer after being managing director and head of the investment banking division.

Perella gained fame as a deal maker during the 1980s along with Bruce Wasserstein at their firm Wasserstein Perella & Co. But their firm's fortunes shrank with the collapse of the junk bond market and the decline in mergers and acquisitions early this decade.
Morgan Stanley said Terry Meguid, a managing director, would replace Perella as head of corporate finance.
The company said Kenneth Deregt, a managing director, would head the bank's fixed-income, or bond, unit.
Neal Garonzik, in charge of Morgan Stanley's equities, or stock, division, is retiring and will be replaced by Vikram Pandit, another managing director.

The bank said the securities business would consist of the equity, fixed-income and investment banking divisions. The securities business will be headed by Peter Karches, a managing director who currently runs the fixed-income division.

The asset management business will include Morgan Stanley Asset Management, Miller Anderson & Sherrerd, Van Kampen American Capital, Private Client Services, Merchant Banking and Morgan Stanley Services.
It will be run by James Allwin, a managing director and president of Morgan Stanley Asset Management.
Morgan Stanley stock dropped 50 cents to $4.625 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Morgan Stanley has a network of 27 principal offices in 19 countries from which it offers financial services to governments, corporations, institutions and individuals.
